text: Change data capture, streamed — every row-level change in a database, as its own live event.
CDC records every insert, update, and delete as it happens. A streamed CDC event carries the operation type, the row's state before and after, and exactly when the change happened.
Databricks lesson 22 covered batch merge — comparing a snapshot on a schedule. Streamed CDC solves the same problem continuously, seeing every change in order instead of a periodic diff.
Repeatedly polling a live production database for changes adds real load to it. CDC instead reads the database's own change log, which it's already maintaining anyway — no extra query load at all.
Continuous sync, no extra load on the source. Next up: real-time data quality — catching bad data before it spreads.
